embeds.title: 🇺🇸 Fed holds at 3.75–4.00%, two officials wanted a hike · 🟡 Mixed for markets
embeds.description:
**Decision: HOLD at 3.75%–4.00% · Forecast hold (4.00% top) · Previous 3.75%–4.00% · Vote 10–2**
The Federal Funds Rate is the rate banks charge each other overnight. The Fed (the US central bank) sets it, and it flows into every loan, mortgage and bond yield. The FOMC is the Fed committee that votes on it. Note: the chair is now Kevin Warsh (not Powell), and he gave the press conference.

fields.name: 🟢🔴 Good or bad news?
fields.value: In line on the number: a hold was fully expected after September's hike. The surprise was hawkish (hawkish = leaning toward higher rates to fight inflation). Two voters, Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed's Hammack, dissented (voted against) because they wanted another 0.25% hike now. The statement upgraded growth from "solid" to "strong" and kept "inflation remains elevated". It added: "The Committee will deliver price stability." The twist: a strong economy is good news, but it gives the Fed room to hike again. Higher rates hurt Nasdaq most. Stocks still rose, so the market read it as a calm hold, not a shock.

fields.name: 🏛️ What it means for the economy
fields.value: Growth is strong (Atlanta Fed's GDPNow estimate: about 3.4% for Q3), jobs are steady, but inflation is too high: headline CPI ran 3.7% a year in September, pushed by oil above $100. Warsh said policy is starting to work and the Fed wants "more information" before the next step. He refused to promise anything about December (no forward guidance, meaning no hints about future moves). Futures markets now lean toward one more hike in December (9 Dec), possibly more in 2027. Rate cuts look far away. Also new: from 2027, one of the eight yearly meetings will be strategy-only, with no rate vote.

fields.name: 📈 Nasdaq (NQ) & S&P (ES)
fields.value: Short term, neutral to slightly positive: no hike today, and Warsh sounded patient. The bigger headwind is the 10-year yield above 5%. The 10-year yield is what the US government pays to borrow for 10 years, and it sets the cost of money for everyone. When it rises, future tech profits are worth less today, so NQ suffers more than ES. Tonight's real driver is Big Tech earnings (Microsoft, Alphabet reported after the close), not the Fed.

fields.name: 🇯🇵 Nikkei (NKD) & yen (6J)
fields.value: 6J barely moved: USD/JPY closed flat near 157.9 (so 6J flat). A wide gap between US and Japanese rates keeps the yen weak, because money flows to where it earns more. A weak yen helps the Nikkei: exporters like Toyota earn dollars that convert into more yen. Risk: near 158, Japan may step in to support the yen. A sudden 6J jump would weigh on NKD. A December Fed hike would keep the yen soft, which supports NKD.

fields.name: 🛢️ Commodities & metals
fields.value: Gold usually dislikes higher rates (it pays no interest), but it held up, +0.4% near $4,078, helped by a softer dollar during the press conference and inflation worries. Crude (CL) is the main inflation driver: about $101.5 at the close (+1.3%), after touching ~$103.5. Expensive oil keeps the Fed hawkish. Silver tends to follow gold. Copper likes strong growth, and the Fed called growth strong, so that supports it, but higher rates are a drag over time. No Fed-specific move in hogs or grains.

fields.name: 📊 How markets actually reacted
fields.value: By the close (investingLive): S&P 500 +0.28% to 7,744. Nasdaq 100 +0.55% to 29,813. US 2-year yield −1 bp to 4.72%, 10-year +5 bp to 5.04%: the curve steepened (short rates fell, long rates rose). bp = basis point = 0.01%. Dollar slipped during the press conference, mixed on the day. USD/JPY flat at 157.94 (6J flat). Gold +0.4% (~$4,078). Crude +1.3% (~$101.5). An intraday snapshot (Yahoo) showed Nasdaq −0.2% and gold −0.6% before both recovered. Nikkei futures: no clear reaction found.

fields.name: 🧭 Bias takeaway
fields.value: The Fed gave no new push either way. It is a hawkish hold, with rates staying high and maybe one more hike in December. That is a mild headwind for NQ (watch the 10-year near 5%), a mild support for NKD while the yen stays weak, and a supportive backdrop for crude and gold while inflation is the story. Conviction is low: Big Tech earnings tonight, the US midterms (3 Nov) and the next CPI report matter more. A cooler CPI or falling oil would ease the hike talk and help NQ. Japanese action to support the yen would hit NKD.

footer.text: Sources: Federal Reserve, Yahoo Finance, investingLive. Context, not signals. Not advice.

embeds.title: 🏦 Hedge fund positioning · week to Tue 20 Oct
embeds.description:
**What this is:** every Friday the US regulator (the CFTC) publishes the **Commitments of Traders (COT)** report: who holds which futures as of the Tuesday before. We watch the **hedge funds** (called *managed money* in commodities, *leveraged funds* in indices and currencies) because they chase trends with big money.

**How to read it:** *net long* = more bets on price going up than down. The **percentile** compares today with the last 3 years: 95th = more bullish than 95% of the time. Above 90th or below 10th = a **crowded trade**: nearly everyone who wants in is already in, so there's little fuel left that way and a sharp **squeeze** the other way gets likely when price turns (losing funds rush to exit). **Commercials** are producers and users (farmers, miners, oil firms). When they sit at the opposite extreme to funds, that's the classic COT setup.

**This week's headlines:**
1. **Commodities are where the extremes are.** Hogs, natural gas and silver have funds at or near their most bearish in 3 years, with commercials heavily long: squeeze fuel.
2. **Crude and gold: funds are light**, commercials at 3-year highs. Room for funds to buy back in.
3. **Nasdaq is the one crowded long** (94th pct), and soybeans too: less fuel left upward.

Next report: Saturday about 6:30am Sydney.

embeds.title: 🇺🇸 US Q3 GDP & Sept Core PCE · 🟡 Mixed for markets (strong growth, sticky inflation, Fed hike risk stays)
embeds.description:
**GDP: Actual 3.4% · Forecast 3.2% · Previous 2.2% (Q2, revised; calendar showed 1.5%)**
**Core PCE m/m: Actual 0.3% · Forecast 0.3% · Previous 0.2%** (y/y 3.1%, as expected; headline PCE +0.5% m/m, 3.6% y/y)

GDP (gross domestic product) is the total value of everything the US produced, shown as an annualised growth rate. Core PCE is the Fed's favourite inflation gauge: price changes on what people buy, minus jumpy food and energy. Traders care because together they tell the Fed whether to raise, hold or cut rates.

fields.name: 🟢🔴 Good or bad news?
fields.value: Growth beat (3.4% vs 3.2%, the fastest in a year per Bloomberg), driven by consumer spending and AI investment. Inflation landed exactly as expected, but 3.1% core is still well above the Fed's 2% goal. The twist: a strong economy is good for company profits, but it gives the Fed no reason to cut and some reason to hike. Higher rates hurt richly priced tech (Nasdaq) the most.

fields.name: 🏛️ What it means for the economy
fields.value: Growth is strong, inflation is stuck around 3%, and there is no sign of the economy cooling. The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on Wednesday after hiking in September, with two members voting for another hike, and upgraded its view of the economy to 'strong'. Futures priced roughly an 81-87% chance of a December hike before this data. Nothing here argues against it. Next test: the Employment Cost Index (wage growth) on Friday.

fields.name: 📈 Nasdaq (NQ) & S&P (ES)
fields.value: Mild headwind. Strong growth supports earnings, but 'higher for longer' rates and a 10-year yield near 5% (the yield is the interest rate on 10-year government bonds) compress tech valuations. NQ was already down about 1% pre-data on a weak Alphabet report. The in-line core number removes the worst-case scare, so the data alone is not a big new sell signal. ES holds up better than NQ.

fields.name: 🇯🇵 Nikkei (NKD) & yen (6J)
fields.value: Strong US data plus Fed hike risk keeps US yields high, which supports the dollar and weighs on the yen (6J down). USD/JPY was trading near 158, so the yen is already weak. A weaker yen usually helps the Nikkei because exporters like Toyota earn more when they convert dollar sales back to yen. Watch the Bank of Japan decision due Fri 30 Oct: a surprise hike would lift 6J and hit NKD.

fields.name: 🛢️ Commodities & metals
fields.value: Gold: hurt by high rates and a firm dollar (gold pays no interest, so it loses appeal when bonds pay 5%). It slid about 1% pre-data to near $4,035. Silver follows gold but also has an industrial side. Copper and crude like strong growth, so 3.4% GDP is mildly supportive, but crude (WTI near $101) is driven more by the Middle East conflict and fell about 1-2% today. Hogs/grains: no direct link.

embeds.title: 🇪🇺 ECB rate decision, statement & Lagarde press conference · ⚪ In line for euro-area markets (hold, hike door left open)
embeds.description:
**Decision: HOLD · Main refinancing rate 2.65% (forecast 2.65%, previous 2.65%) · Deposit rate 2.50%**
The ECB (European Central Bank) sets the cost of money for the 20 euro countries. The deposit rate is what banks earn parking cash at the ECB; it is the rate markets watch most. The ECB has hiked twice this year (June, Sept) to fight an oil-driven inflation jump (euro inflation 3.8% in Sept, target 2%). Big side story: Lagarde announced today she will step down early, on 7 Feb 2027.

fields.name: 🟢🔴 Good or bad news?
fields.value: Exactly as expected, so no shock. The tone leaned hawkish (hawkish = leaning toward higher rates): Lagarde said energy prices rose more than staff forecast in September and headline inflation will stay well above target for the coming quarters. Reports say the council even debated hiking today. But the statement also said financing conditions have tightened and wages show no real reaction yet, which softens the urgency. Net: in line, with a December hike still the base case.

fields.name: 🏛️ What it means for the economy
fields.value: Europe faces stagflation risk: an energy shock (Middle East war, Brent near $115) pushes prices up while hurting growth. The ECB said the bigger, longer shock likely lifts inflation and lowers growth. Next step: markets price a hike to 2.75% on 10 Dec (new forecasts then) and about three hikes in total by end-2027 (deposit rate 3.25%). A pause would need energy prices to fall. Lagarde's exit adds a leadership question but analysts expect little market impact.

fields.name: 📈 Nasdaq (NQ) & S&P (ES)
fields.value: Small direct effect. Europe hiking while the Fed holds (3.75-4.00%, two dissenters wanted a hike yesterday) keeps the global message 'rates stay high', a mild headwind for expensive tech. Today's real driver is Alphabet's earnings (AI spending fears), not the ECB. A weaker euro means a firmer dollar, slightly negative for US multinationals. Lean: neutral-to-mildly bearish from this event alone.

fields.name: 🇯🇵 Nikkei (NKD) & yen (6J)
fields.value: Little direct knock-on. 6J is yen futures: 6J up = yen stronger. The yen stays weak (USD/JPY about 157.8), so 6J is low; a weak yen helps the Nikkei because exporters like Toyota earn more when foreign sales convert back to yen. Global central banks staying hawkish keeps yield gaps wide versus Japan, which tends to keep the yen soft. Watch for Japan's finance ministry warning about yen weakness near 158-160: intervention would spike 6J and hit NKD.

fields.name: 🛢️ Commodities & metals
fields.value: Crude (CL): the ECB is reacting to oil, not moving it. WTI about $101-102 is driven by Middle East supply risk. Gold (GC) & silver (SI): hawkish banks everywhere and a firmer dollar are headwinds, since gold pays no interest and is priced in dollars. Copper (HG): Europe's growth warning is mildly negative; copper likes strong growth. Hogs/grains: no direct link.

fields.name: 📊 How markets actually reacted
fields.value: Reports say markets 'did not move much' on the decision. Euro -0.3% to about $1.11, lowest since May (dollar firmer). STOXX 600 +0.95%. Euro 2-year yields fell. US: Nasdaq -1.9% and S&P -0.6% after the open, mostly on Alphabet. US 10-year yield 4.95% from 5.05% late Wed. Gold about $4,040 (-0.3%). WTI about $101.5 (-1.3%). Yen and Nikkei: no clear reaction found.

fields.name: 🏦 Hedge funds (COT)
fields.value:
As of 20 Oct: NQ funds net +950, 94th pct, Crowded long. Hawkish rates plus tech selling push AGAINST this crowd: squeeze risk lower if they exit fast.
GC funds net +104k, 24th pct, Leaning short. Firm dollar goes WITH the light positioning, but there is not much left to sell.
SI funds net +3.5k, 3rd pct, Crowded short. Bearish news has little fuel left; any good surprise could force a sharp short squeeze up.
6J funds net -22.9k, 74th pct, Neutral. No crowding signal either way.

fields.name: 🧭 Bias takeaway
fields.value: The ECB adds a mild 'higher for longer' tilt but is not today's main mover. For NQ, a crowded fund long plus hawkish banks plus AI-earnings worries supports a cautious-to-bearish lean over the next days, moderate strength; a drop in oil or softer US inflation would change it. NKD stays supported by the weak yen unless Japan intervenes. For metals, the dollar is a headwind but silver's crowded short makes chasing shorts risky.

embeds.title: 🇯🇵 BoJ Rate Decision, Statement & Outlook Report · ⚪ In line for the yen & Japanese markets (hawkish tilt)
embeds.description:
**Decision: HOLD at 1.25% · Forecast <1.25% · Previous 1.25% · Vote 8-1 (Takata wanted 1.5%)**
The Bank of Japan (BoJ) sets Japan's short-term interest rate. Higher rates usually mean a stronger yen and tighter money. Its quarterly Outlook Report now sees core inflation (prices minus fresh food) at 2.5% this fiscal year and 2.6% next (raised from 2.4%), with growth near 0.7%. New wording: underlying inflation is 'generally consistent' with the 2% target. Traders care because it decides how fast Japan keeps hiking, which drives 6J and the Nikkei.

fields.name: 🟢🔴 Good or bad news?
fields.value: In line on the rate, slightly hawkish in the details. Hawkish = leaning toward higher rates. Three hawkish bits: the BoJ now says its 2% inflation goal is basically met, one member (Takata) voted for a hike to 1.5%, and it will sell its stock ETFs 2.6x faster from Jan 2027 (another form of tightening). But no surprise hike and only one dissenter, so some desks called it a dovish (soft) hold. Good for yen bulls, mildly bad for Japanese stocks.

fields.name: 🏛️ What it means for the economy
fields.value: Japan has steady inflation around 2-2.7% and slow growth (about 0.7% a year). The BoJ now says its job is to stop inflation running above 2%, not to escape deflation. Risks it named: higher energy prices, AI-related demand and a weak yen. Markets priced about 80% odds of a hike to 1.50% at the 18-19 Dec meeting before today, and nothing here pushes against that. Base case: hold now, hike in December, then slowly toward a 'neutral' rate (one that neither speeds up nor slows the economy).

fields.name: 📈 Nasdaq (NQ) & S&P (ES)
fields.value: Small direct effect. The BoJ matters to US stocks through the 'yen carry trade': funds borrow cheap yen to buy US assets. Faster Japanese hikes can force them to unwind and sell. A December hike, flagged in advance, is a slow risk, not a shock. The real driver for NQ today is the AI spending scare after Amazon and Intel results, not Tokyo. ES follows NQ but drops less.

fields.name: 🇯🇵 Nikkei (NKD) & yen (6J)
fields.value: 6J: hawkish hints and a December hike support a firmer yen (6J up). The gap between US and Japanese rates is slowly narrowing. The 157-160 per-dollar zone is where Tokyo has stepped in to buy yen before, which caps how weak it can get. NKD: a stronger yen weighs on the Nikkei because exporters (Toyota, Sony, chip-gear makers) earn less when overseas profits convert back to fewer yen. Faster ETF sales add a small extra headwind from 2027.

fields.name: 🛢️ Commodities & metals
fields.value: Little direct impact. Gold likes a weaker US dollar; a firmer yen softens the dollar a bit, a mild plus. The BoJ cited energy prices as an inflation risk, with WTI crude near $103. Japan is a big crude importer, so a stronger yen makes oil cheaper for it, but it does not move global oil prices much. Copper follows China and AI/data-centre demand more than the BoJ. Hogs and grains: no link.

fields.name: 📊 How markets actually reacted
fields.value: Calm. Yen about 0.2% firmer near 157.4-157.5 per dollar (6J slightly up); crosses like GBP/JPY barely moved. Nikkei cash around -2.4% (about 63,100), but that was the AI tech selloff that started before the decision. NQ futures about -1.4% and US 10-year yield down ~7bp to about 4.91% on the same AI scare. Gold about $4,009 (-0.6%), WTI about $103.4 (+1.4%). Ueda's press conference is 3:30pm Tokyo (5:30pm Sydney); expect a second move then.

fields.name: 🏦 Hedge funds (COT)
fields.value: As of 20 Oct. 6J: funds net -22,890 short, 74th percentile, Neutral, but they added about 30k shorts in 4 weeks. A hawkish BoJ pushes AGAINST that new short, so a short squeeze (fast buying back) could lift the yen. NKD: +575, 22nd pct, Leaning short; little long fuel, room to fall further. NQ: +950, 94th pct, Crowded long; the AI scare pushes AGAINST it, so more forced selling is possible. GC: +104k, 24th pct, Leaning short; room to run if the dollar slips.

fields.name: 🧭 Bias takeaway
fields.value: Mild bullish lean for the yen (6J) into December, helped by funds' recent shorts. Mild bearish lean for NKD, mostly from the AI selloff, with a firmer yen adding pressure. NQ stays driven by AI earnings, and crowded longs make it fragile. This changes if Ueda plays down December at 5:30pm Sydney: the yen would weaken and NKD would bounce. Commodities: neutral, no BoJ-driven bias.

footer.text: Sources: investingLive, Investing.com, EconoTimes, Reuters, CNBC. Context, not signals. Not advice.

embeds.title: 🇯🇵 BOJ Press Conference (Ueda) · ⏳ Not found yet
embeds.description:
**Ueda's press conference comments: not found yet.** I searched for about 25 minutes after it started (3:30pm Tokyo / 5:30pm Sydney) and found no reliable write-up of what he said about the next hike, the yen or bond buying. I won't guess.

**Confirmed earlier today, from two sources: the decision itself.** The BOJ (Bank of Japan, Japan's central bank) kept its policy rate (the interest rate it sets for short-term borrowing) at 1.25%. The vote was 8-1: board member Takata wanted a hike to 1.5%. The statement said underlying inflation (price rises once one-off swings like energy are removed) is now 'generally consistent' with the 2% target. Risks to prices lean to the upside. The FY2027 core inflation forecast went up to 2.6% from 2.4%. The BOJ will also sell its stock ETFs (funds that track the stock market) more than twice as fast from January 2027: about ¥860bn a year, up from ¥330bn.

**Why it matters:** these are hawkish signals (pointing to higher rates). Before the meeting, around 80% of economists expected a hike at the 18 December meeting. Early reaction: the yen firmed (6J up) to about 157.1 per dollar. Watch Ueda's comments for confirmation of a December hike.
